title: The Better Temple
summary: Fire fell and glory filled Solomon's temple, but that temple was destroyed. In Christ we have the eternal temple and the eternal King.
exhortation: This passage recounts the dedication of Solomon's temple, which 1 Kings 6:1 tells us was 480 years after the Israelites left Egypt. Centuries. For all that time the people of Israel had worshiped the Lord in tents. They had been promised a land and an inheritance of children, but they wandered, struggled, fought and died.

And here, finally, was the moment they had long awaited. Their great King David, whose whole heart belonged to God, had defeated their enemies and brought peace to the land, the salvation they longed for. Now his son Solomon had built the temple with all the gold, wood and stone David had stored up: a permanent, strong house for the Lord. No longer a tent. Fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifice, as if God were saying, "This is the temple. I will live here." His glory filled the temple with such brilliance that the people fell on their faces in worship. Surely this is where God will dwell forever, they must have thought.
But as great as it was, it was not the fulfillment of the promise. That temple was destroyed. The worship ceased. The people were scattered and broken, and the king died.

But friends, we live in the time when the prophecies and promises are fulfilled. In Christ we have the eternal temple. In Christ we have the eternal King. The glory we see in him will never fade, and one day we will stare into its brilliance without blinking, with bodies made to endure it and enjoy it forever. So, Lord, let your glory fall. Let your fire consume all sin and double-mindedness in us, so that we worship you in spirit and truth with a whole heart, refined by that fire and made ready for your kingdom, our hearts overflowing in awe and wonder.
prayer: Lord, soften the hearts that need to be softened. Break the hearts that need to be broken, and restore the hearts that need to be lifted up. Remind your people who you are and what they were made for.

Our hearts are longing for your presence, and for your Spirit to break through where there is coldness and deadness and no turning toward you. We need your Spirit to break through in powerful and mighty ways. Come, Spirit of God, and awaken our hearts. In Jesus' name.
